title: Trigonometric Parameter Elimination and Elliptical Motion
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Eliminate the parameter t from x = 4*cos(t), y = 3*sin(t) for 0 <= t <= 2*pi, identify the resulting Cartesian curve, and specify its orientation.

steps.title: Isolate the Trigonometric Functions
steps.explanation: Divide the parametric equations by their respective semi-axis coefficients.
steps.why: Isolating trigonometric functions enables the application of the fundamental Pythagorean identity.

steps.title: Apply the Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Square both equations and add them together, eliminating t entirely.
steps.why: The identity cos^2(t) + sin^2(t) = 1 eliminates the parameter without introducing extraneous roots.

steps.title: Determine Traversal Orientation
steps.explanation: At t = 0, the curve is at (4,0). As t increases to pi/2, the position moves to (0,3). This sequence confirms the trajectory travels counterclockwise around the origin.
steps.why: Evaluating sequential parameter values identifies the directional orientation of parametric motion.
